messages.content: Explain why the sky appears blue during the day and red near sunset. Keep the answer concise.
Give three practical suggestions for making a small software project easier for a new contributor to understand.
Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that returns overlapping closed intervals merged in sorted order. Include type hints and tests.
Implement a Rust function that checks whether brackets in a UTF-8 string are balanced for (), [], and {}. Explain its time and space complexity.

Summarize the following project note into five bullets, preserving decisions, evidence, and unresolved risks.

A research team is evaluating an inference optimization. The unoptimized system is the reference because it is simple and already used in production. The proposed system adds a smaller draft model that suggests several future tokens. A larger target model verifies all suggestions and rejects any that do not match its distribution. This preserves the target distribution, but speed is not guaranteed: the draft consumes compute and memory, and benefits depend on how frequently its proposals are accepted. Code and repetitive text may produce high agreement; open-ended dialogue may not. The team will measure client-observed time to first token, average time per output token, tail latency, output throughput, acceptance rate, and GPU memory. Tests must use identical prompts and generation settings. Each configuration will be warmed up and repeated. Results from individual requests are not treated as independent experimental replicates; deployment-level repeats are the unit of comparison. The final recommendation must distinguish low-concurrency latency from throughput under load. It must also disclose failures, counter resets, prompt-set limitations, and any configuration that changes available KV-cache capacity.

Read the following incident narrative and produce: (1) a short chronology, (2) the root cause, (3) contributing factors, and (4) corrective actions.

An API deployment passed its model-list health check at 10:02. The upstream inference worker was still loading weights, but the gateway advertised the model immediately. A load generator began at 10:03 and every request received HTTP 503. Operators initially classified the result as model saturation because the planned request rate was high. GPU telemetry showed no active kernels and queue metrics were empty. At 10:09 the worker completed initialization and manual completions succeeded. Investigation showed that readiness was based only on registration in the gateway, not on a successful generation. The benchmark record was discarded. The workflow was changed to require a real, short chat completion after model discovery and before warmup. Unavailability and load-generator exhaustion were also separated from performance failures so neither could move the estimated serving-capacity boundary.
